thread_title: S. flava var. ornata 'dipped lip' Liberty Co, FL
breadcrumb: S. flava var. ornata 'dipped lip' Liberty Co, FL

posts.body_html:
This plant has been in the collection for probably over a decade now, and it hasn't been noticed until now! Is it me, or does this clone have a somewhat Reptilian look to it?! Maybe I'm just seeing things....Anyways, what's interesting is how in the throat of this plant, there's a red line that goes vertically, much like what you see in the bulloch Co, GA black veined ornata variants. I haven't really noticed this characteristic outside the bulloch Co, GA plants until now.

S. flava var. ornata 'dipped lip' Liberty Co, FL, photos taken Cinco De Mayo-DIA DE LOS MUERTOS!!!! (bueno, todos los dias es el dia los Muertos para los insectos y para aquellos que fuman tabaco), 2018:


The lips on this thing are slightly exaggerated on this particular trap, I think it didn't quite open up right:

posts.body_html:
Really loving this clone, even though it doesn't really look that impressive...yet. Last year's traps were a bit more ornate, so maybe it's the potential of the plant that brings about excitement. I = think it needs to produce big traps before you see all the characteristics at their maximum glory. Have I ever seen this plant produce big traps? Nope, not yet, just sharing some wishful thinking with yall! It was stunted in a community tray for eons, transplanted mid last season, and now has a full season to be babied for Corey (bog Jesus Ladies and Gentlemen). Photos taken 6/17/19:




Oh, and for your flower geeks, that's a Lilium irridollae flower spike to the right of the trap! Haven't written a thread on this endangered lily just yet, but if it snaps out of some funk that it's in and ends up blooming, you will see a little story about it in the near future on this forum:
